thread:
Leah: FYI — nightly playbook sweep flagged ~4.8k accounts for 're-onboard' flows overnight. Looks like suppression TTL + healthscore bounce -> churn. Anyone else seeing a spike? :eyes:
Mateo: Whoa, that many? Can you paste the sweep summary?
Leah: Yep — hygiene-bot posted this at 02:03: 
```
[hygiene-bot] playbook-sweep 2025-09-14 02:03:12
- total candidates: 4876
- triggered: 4129
- suppressed by TTL: 3792
- re-triggers (last 30d): 2314
- dry-run flag: true
```
Leah: Context: we set suppression TTL to 7 days for low-touch accounts earlier this year. Looks like healthscore decays then bounces after telemetry backfills -> playbook thinks they're newly risky.
Priya: Thanks for surfacing. This would increase noise for CS owners a lot. Any quick mitigation besides extending TTL?
Ivy: Can we add a confidence check on telemetry completeness before re-triggering? e.g., require 48h of stable telemetry after a gap.
Mateo: Agree on confidence guard. Also suggest a soft-mark: instead of full playbook, enqueue a lightweight 'verify' step that pings owner and waits 24h. If owner doesn't act, escalate. That reduces churn.
Leah: Proposal: 3-part plan
1) Run a targeted dry-run for accounts with "last-active < 14d AND healthscore delta > 20" to measure true positives.
2) Add a telemetry-stability gate: require two consistent samples 24h apart before full playbook.
3) Add a temporary cohort TTL bump from 7d -> 21d while we roll changes (2-week canary).
Mateo: Can do the dry-run query now. Running: 
```sql
SELECT account_id, last_active, healthscore_delta, owner_id
FROM cs_candidates
WHERE last_active BETWEEN now() - interval '30 days' AND now() - interval '2 days'
AND healthscore_delta > 20;
```
Mateo: Initial dry-run result: 4,876 rows (same ballpark). Random sampling (n=100) shows ~66% false re-triggers where telemetry backfill caused spike.
Leah: Good to know. So we should avoid mass re-trigger. Priya — do you want the canary TTL increase or do we run the telemetry gate first?
Priya: Let's gate first (less customer-facing change). Implement telemetry-stability gate + verify-step. If noise still > 15% after 72h, then bump TTL as a fallback.
Ivy: For rollout: can we ship config flag 'playbook.retrigger.confidence' default=2-samples, sample-interval=24h, and make it pageable per-playbook?
Mateo: Yep I can add config. Suggest feature-flag it behind cs-toggle so we can flip per-tenant. Will need a migration to default safe values.
Leah: I'll prepare a short runbook for CS owners explaining the change and the 'verify' lightweight step so they don't panic.
Priya: Add metrics to track: daily triggers, re-triggers within 30d, owner-ack time, false-positive rate (manual labels from CS). We'll monitor in the Console.
hygiene-bot: dry-run-summary posted. counts: total:4876, sample-false-positive-rate:66%, owners-impacted: 1322.
Leah: Action items: @Mateo - implement gate + verify-step behind feature flag (ETA 48h). @Ivy - help scope owner notification content. @Priya - confirm monitoring dashboard (SLO: false-positive < 15%). I'll coordinate owner comms.
Mateo: Got it, starting branch now. Will ping when dry-run endpoint is available. :thumbsup:
Ivy: I'll draft the owner note and send for review.
Priya: Thanks team. If we see owner backlash, we revert flag and push TTL bump as hotfix.
Leah: Keeping this as dry-run + canary. Will post progress in this thread.
Mateo: 02:18 update — branch pushed, feature flag created: cs.playbook.retrigger.confidence (int samples, interval hours). Endpoint: /internal/playbook/dry-run?flag=confidence_test
Leah: Nice. Leaving trial to run overnight, will sample owners tomorrow morning and report.
Ivy: Appreciate it.
Leah: End of thread update (02:29) — removing immediate mass requeue, will not push any full re-triggers until canary completes.
